context: The full lattice isometry group is often denoted \(\mathrm{Co}_0=2.\mathrm{Co}_1\). It has twice this order and is not the simple group \(\mathrm{Co}_1\).

The action on 100 points is transitive. A point stabilizer has orbits of sizes \(1,22,77\); the invariant graph from the orbit of length 22 is the Higman–Sims graph. Its full automorphism group is \(\mathrm{HS}:2\), so \(\mathrm{HS}\) has index two in that larger group.

The Hall–Janko graph has 100 vertices and valency 36. Its full automorphism group is \(J_2:2\); \(J_2\) is the simple subgroup of index two. The graph is not uniquely specified by its strongly regular parameters alone.

The action is transitive and a point stabilizer has orbits of sizes \(1,112,162\), giving a rank-three action. The stabilizer is isomorphic to the projective special unitary group \(\mathrm{PSU}_4(3)\).

The finite simple groups of Lie type \({}^2B_2(q)\), for \(q=2^{2m+1}\) with integer \(m\ge1\), are also called Suzuki groups. That parameterized family is distinct from the sporadic group \(\mathrm{Suz}\). Likewise, the central covers \(2.\mathrm{Suz}\), \(3.\mathrm{Suz}\), and \(6.\mathrm{Suz}\) are distinct groups.
